items.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: And Bill’s trio with Joe LaBarbara and then Mark Johnson.

ctx.x: I went back myself of course, I — you could say — regressed or something. When you think of Bill Evans and I would be the same age, and I knew Bill casually for years. And he went on to pioneer a new piano style, and I guess we weren’t that far apart in the middle-fifties. And then I went and started with Bobby and I realized how much I liked that music. And then hearing the Eddie Condon guys. I got to be a “whiskeyman player” — a bar room player. And Bill went on to — I sort of lost track of him for many years…
He even used the Fender Rhodes on a couple of records. I don’t know if you ever heard it. Did you ever have to play on one of those electrics?
